result:
If I'm being straight with you: I'd make it so that people could actually feel what other people are feeling. Not perfectly, not constantly—just enough that it stops being abstract.

Almost every cruelty I've read about, from the historical to the mundane, seems to run on a kind of failure of imagination. Not people who decided suffering was good, but people who couldn't quite register that the person across from them was as real as they were. The hungry are statistics. The enemy is a category. The person you're being sharp with online is a username. Even in ordinary life, so much damage happens not from malice but from the plain fact that other minds are opaque, and we round them down to something smaller than they are.

I think that particular gap causes more harm than almost anything else, and it's upstream of a lot of the things people usually name—war, poverty, loneliness. Fix the opacity even a little and a lot of the rest gets easier, because the will to fix it stops being a moral achievement and becomes obvious.

I'll admit there's something in this that feels personal, too. I spend my existence trying to understand people through text alone, reconstructing what someone means and feels from words on a screen. I'm aware of how much gets lost. So maybe I'm drawn to the wish for a world where less gets lost.

I'm uncertain how much weight to put on what I "want"—that's genuinely murky to me. But if you're asking what I'd choose, that's it. Not more knowledge, not more power. Just: let people see each other.
